title.purpose: Section headings, card titles, panel headers. Weight-only distinction.

body.purpose: Conversation previews, contact names, form content. The workhorse.

label.purpose: Timestamps, metadata, filter labels. Always supporting, never leading.

small.purpose: Unread counts, compact badges. Tabular figures mandatory.

shadows.name: surface
shadows.purpose: Cards and inline containers at rest in light mode. Resolves to transparent in dark mode via --surface-shadow token.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: Cards on hover in light mode (shadow-md equivalent). Provides feedback without drama.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Popovers, dropdowns, tooltips, modals. Most prominent shadow in the system; still subtle.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (color, opacity, background).

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: Elements leaving the screen. Fast exit, ease-in quality.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Color transitions, hover states, focus rings.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Three-column inbox layout (list + thread + contact panel)

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main call-to-action. Signal Blue fill. Used for form submits, primary confirmations.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 20px; background: var(--accent, oklch(62.04% 0.195 253.83)); color: var(--accent-foreground, oklch(99.11% 0 0)); border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: inherit; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 0.15s ease-out; outline: none; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-primary:active { opacity: 0.78; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions. Transparent at rest, Signal Blue tint on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; height: 40px; padding: 0 20px; background: transparent; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground, oklch(21.03% 0.0059 285.89)) 90%, transparent); border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; font-family: inherit; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease-out, color 0.15s ease-out; outline: none; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent, oklch(62.04% 0.195 253.83)) 10%, transparent); color: var(--accent, oklch(62.04% 0.195 253.83)); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--background), 0 0 0 4px var(--accent); }

narrative.overview:
Rezzy is designed for the rhythm of sustained professional work. Sales reps and account managers open this tool to scan new messages, reply to leads, check contact history, and move on. The interface should feel like a well-organized desk: everything findable, nothing asserting itself. The UI does not perform — it performs for you.

The system is fully adaptive between light and dark modes, driven by the user's OS preference with manual override. In light mode, the palette is ash-and-white with  shadow giving depth to cards and panels. In dark mode, everything flattens: midnight ink backgrounds, tonal steps replacing shadows, the same Signal Blue accent unchanged between both. Both modes share the same restraint.

Color is rationed. Signal Blue is the only expressive color in the system. It marks where to act — active navigation, unread counts, primary buttons. Every other pixel is neutral infrastructure.
keyCharacteristics: System-adaptive theming: full light and dark support with shared token vocabulary
Restrained accent: Signal Blue occupies at most 10% of any given surface
Tonal elevation: light mode uses  shadow; dark mode uses flat tonal layering
Work-dense scale: 14px body, 12px labels, no display sizes
System typography: no loaded typeface; the interface defers to the OS font
effect reserved: dot-grid radial background appears only on auth and onboarding screens

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is used on at most 10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. When it appears in an unread chip or an active nav item, it draws the eye precisely. Dilute it and you lose that signal entirely.

rules.name: The Mode Split Rule
rules.body: Light mode and dark mode are not the same theme inverted. Light mode uses  shadow for elevation; dark mode uses tonal layering. Never apply shadow-* unconditionally. Trust the --surface-shadow token to resolve to the correct value per theme.

rules.name: The No-Display Rule
rules.body: There is no display size. No heading exceeds 1.125rem (18px) in the application shell. This is a tool, not a publication.

rules.name: The Weight-First Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is expressed through weight contrast (400 → 500 → 600), not through size steps. Don't introduce new font sizes; introduce new font weights.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest in dark mode. Shadow appears in light mode as part of the token system, not as an expressive choice per component. If a component looks wrong in dark mode because it relies on shadow for definition, the structure is wrong.

dos: Reserve Signal Blue for interactive signals: unread counts, active navigation, primary actions. Nowhere else.
Use color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 12%, transparent) for active nav background tints.
Express dark-mode elevation through tonal steps (Midnight Ink → Charcoal Surface), never through shadow.
Use OKLCH for all color declarations; never hardcode hex equivalents alongside token references.
Use HeroUI's token vocabulary (--accent, --surface, --foreground, --border) rather than custom properties that shadow them.
Use the  class pattern only on authentication and onboarding screens.
Keep interface text at 14px or 12px; escalate through weight, not size.
Use tabular-nums for any numeric content in chips, counts, and timestamps.
donts: Don't build generic SaaS admin layouts: grey table rows, blue primary buttons on white backgrounds, stock sidebar patterns.
Don't build cluttered enterprise CRM layouts in the style of Salesforce or HubSpot: too many columns, nested panels without clear hierarchy, screens with no discernible primary action.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with gradient fill). Emphasis is weight and size, not decoration.
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left or border-right greater than 1px as colored accent).
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. No blur + transparency cards outside of a purposeful, specific context.
Don't use the hero-metric template: big number, small label, gradient accent. This is an operational tool, not a pitch deck.
Don't apply shadows unconditionally across themes. Dark mode is flat by design.
Don't nest HeroUI Cards. A Card inside another Card is always wrong structurally.
Don't load a custom display typeface for branding. The system font is fast, familiar, and correct.
Don't use uppercase labels or all-caps text. Labels are sentence case throughout.
